question.worked_solution:
First, we need to find the equation of the parabola. From the diagram, we see that the parabola has a vertex at $(1,-4)$ and passes through the point $(0,-3).$

The general standard equation of an up- or down-opening parabola with vertex $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
(x-h)^{2}=4p(y-k).
$$

Substituting $(h,k)=(1,-4)$ into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =4p(y+4).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we need to find $p.$ Since the parabola passes through the point $(0,-3),$ we substitute $x=0$ and $y=-3$ into the equation and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(0-1)^{2} & =4p(-3+4) \\ 1 & =4p(1) \\ p & =\frac{1}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the parabola is

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =y+4.\end{aligned}
$$

When the parabola intersects the $x$-axis, we must have $y=0.$ So, we substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the parabola and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-1)^{2} & =0+4 \\ (x-1)^{2} & =4 \\ x-1 & =\pm \sqrt{4} \\ x & =\pm 2+1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, from left to right, the $x$-intercepts are $-1$  and $3.$
